title: Generic-point unit for a normal constant sheaf
statement: Let Y be an integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed, let g be the canonical morphism from the generic point of Y, and let M be a module over a commutative ring Λ. The unit from the constant Λ-module sheaf on Y to its pushforward along g is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose an affine open chart Spec R containing the image of a geometric point s. Its stalks are isomorphic to stalks of Y, so R is an integrally closed domain by the normal-stalk criterion. The chart description supplies a local strict-henselization ring C, a chart ring map, and an ind-etale R-algebra structure on C. Apply the official chart theorem at the full affine colimit and transport its ring map and maximal ideal through smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. Its inverse leg equation and the two defining structural-map equations identify the transported structure map with the existing small-model structure map. Where ind-etaleness is used, apply the official chart ind-etale theorem with the spectrum of this comparison isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: Present C as a filtered colimit of etale R-algebras. The etale-colimit normal-local-domain theorem gives IsDomain C and injectivity R→C. Tensoring C with the fraction field of R is localization of C at the images of nonzero elements of R; injectivity ensures these images are nonzero, so this localization is a domain.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: The spectrum of that tensor-product domain is the pullback of the generic point of Spec R and Spec C. Remove the common open-immersion factor in the two pullback legs, then use the open-immersion stalk isomorphism at the generic point to identify this pullback with the strict fibre over the generic point of Y. Thus this fibre is integral and therefore connected.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, degree zero and canonical restriction construction; Tag 09Z5

proof.text: The proved constant-strict-fibre comparison identifies the unit on each geometric stalk with the canonical coefficient map to sections on the strict fibre. The latter is invertible because that fibre is connected: transfer the abelian-group constant-section theorem through ModuleCat→AddCommGrpCat, using preserved sheafification and reflection of isomorphisms. The coefficient germ to the constant-sheaf stalk is invertible directly by the proved generic Point.toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberConstIso_hom and Point.isIso_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify_const API, combined with Point.toPresheafFiber_naturality. This uses the generic coefficient-category result, not the separate abelian-group-specific ConstantSheafGeometricStalk module. Cancel the coefficient germ and the strict-fibre comparison to prove the stalk unit invertible.

proof.text: Transport stalk invertibility through the canonical universe-lifting isomorphism of fibre functors. Apply the conservative family of geometric stalks to obtain IsIso for the original unit, with its statement unchanged.
